previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and diabetic neuropathy was admitted after developing hypotension and dyspnea during dialysis. He later reported chest pressure, palpitations, and nausea, prompting evaluation for acute coronary syndrome. Workup including serial troponins and EKG showed no evidence of myocardial infarction. His symptoms resolved with supportive care, and he remained hemodynamically stable. A left leg ultrasound ruled out DVT, and chest imaging showed stable mild pulmonary edema. He was monitored overnight, required no dialysis during admission, and was discharged back to an extended care facility with no medication changes and instructions to monitor weight and symptoms.

DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE:  The patient was brought in the
operating room, identified by name, medical record number,
and date of birth.  He was placed on the operating table in a
supine position.  After the adequate induction of sedation,
the left upper extremity was circumferentially prepped and
draped in a standard sterile fashion.  A final preoperative
time-out was undertaken to ensure this was, in fact, the
correct patient, site, side, and procedure.

We began by making a 2 cm incision in the antecubital fossa,
which was the incision that we had previously used to band
the fistula.  We dissected through skin and subcutaneous
tissues, and encountered the fistula at the location of the
banding.  This fistula was circumferentially dissected and
then ligated with a ___ silk tie.  This completely occluded
all blood flow.  We then closed the incision with interrupted
___ Vicryl followed by interrupted ___ nylon mattress
sutures.

correct x2. A dry sterile dressing was applied and the aneurysms 
were
milked of their blood forward and then an Ace wrap was used
to compress the fistula to try to keep the aneurysms from
refilling with blood in a retrograde fashion.

outpatient regimen.

# Generalized Pain: Mr ___ had several complaints of pain 
in his legs, shoulder, back, chest, and arms at various times

minimal effect. Palliative care was consulted for pain 
management and nortipyline was added as well. Patient will

Dear Mr ___,

You were originally admitted to the hospital because you were 
having pains while on dialysis and you were unable to finish 
multiple sessions. While admitted, the fistula in your left arm 
was ligated. Your normal dialysis schedule was resumed and you 
were able to tolerate extended sessions without having a 
recurrence of your symptoms. You did, however, continue to have 
pain in other sites so we changed your pain medications and had 
our palliative care service meet with you to determine how best 
to treat your pain and achieve your goals. You are discharged 
home with your new regimen with the intent to follow up with 
your outpatient providers and resume your normally scheduled 
dialysis. Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes 
up more than 3 lbs.

appointments.
